# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 3. Parent = cand_0002 (ACCEPT, val 0.571). Scoring is HARD restriction: the
agent's FINAL code is text-substituted `1_<id>_input`→`2_/3_` and RE-RUN on two hidden
input files (same layout, different data/row-counts); a task counts only if ALL 3 match
answer_position. Signatures: `[1,0,0]`/`[1,0,1]`/`[1,1,0]` = passes preview, fails the
hidden re-run (a generalization/edge-case gap); `[0,0,0]` = wrong on the preview too
(comprehension error or environment fault).

## Diagnosis summary (THIS iteration's ./trajectories/, 39 failing)
cand_0001 and cand_0002 already harvested the CLEAN prose-fixable clusters: the RE-RUN /
generalization block, TYPE/FORMAT, verify-before-finish, BLANK-vs-ZERO, POSITIONAL/exact
semantics, composite-keys, and the example-as-check. I re-read the actual code the agent
now emits on the failing tasks (30930, 32975, 58890, 58484, 269-44, 157-4, 585-41, 45300,
267-18, 353-19, …). The residue is NOT another clean knowledge gap: the gen-gap solutions
are already well-generalized (dynamic headers, last-row detection, composite keys), so the
failures are subtle **boundary/edge-case** bugs and genuine **comprehension** errors, plus
a handful of **environment faults**. No ground-truth is present in the traces or working
dir, so comprehension-error clusters cannot be VERIFIED (I cannot confirm the correct
interpretation without gold) — editing for them would fail the VERIFIED/SAFE tests. I
therefore shipped only the two edits I can verify from the traces and defend as bounded,
and I document the plateau honestly rather than padding with speculative prose (which, on
an already-long prompt read by a model less robust on long context, risks dilution).

## Ranked issue list (biggest leverage first)
| rank | cluster | tasks (evidence) | root cause | tag | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Generalization boundary/edge-cases in run/segment computations | 30930 [1,0,0], 32975 [1,0,0], 58890 [1,0,0], 58484 [1,0,0], 42930 [1,0,0], 250-20 [1,0,1], 49782 [1,0,1], 53305 [1,0,1] | Code handles only the fully-enclosed middle segments / the marker rows it saw in the preview; a hidden file that starts or ends mid-segment (leading/trailing partial segment, back-to-back markers, marker-row inclusion) drops or misplaces values | KNOWLEDGE (additive, narrowing to run/segment tasks) | **Edit B**: extend the contiguous-run bullet with the boundary cases to cover (prompt.md) |
| 2 | Unattended-re-run crash → no output on a hidden variant | 353-19 (`[1,0,1]`, case 2 "produced NO output file — code never wrote output_path") | Dynamic code raised on a differently-shaped hidden input and aborted before saving | KNOWLEDGE + STRUCTURE | **Edit A**: robustness rule — code must run to completion and save unconditionally on inputs it never saw (prompt.md) |
| — | Comprehension / ambiguous-spec errors (`[0,0,0]`) | 269-44, 34-5, 157-4, 577-40, 398-14, 413-15, 146-49, 267-18, 254-34, 36478, 45300, 18137, 50526, 55912, 39946, 32468, 53449, 55039, 10281, 577-40, 6698, 14207, 50486, 585-41 | Wrong reading of an underspecified instruction; the emitted code already generalizes but implements the wrong operation. No general prose rule fixes these without leaking a task-specific interpretation, and there is no gold in the traces to VERIFY a direction. | SKIPPED (unverifiable) | not edited |
| — | Volatile "current date" | 34-5, 32023 | "current month"/TODAY() resolves differently at grade time vs benchmark creation | SKIPPED | not edited |
| — | Environment / eval faults | 45944 (known recalc), 53062 (48k-row recalc), 4225 & 55258 (output provably reproduces the instruction's own stated example yet [0,0,0] — grader/type-coercion fault) | Infra, not a prompt defect | ENVIRONMENT (handed back) | not worked around |

## Changes made this iteration (both ADDITIVE — no global rule loosened, no deletion)
| edit | class | file | what & why it generalizes | blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule, narrowing) | prompt.md | Extend the "runs of / delimited by / between-within markers" bullet: also handle the partial segment BEFORE the first marker and AFTER the last marker (a segment with no closing marker still needs its result), back-to-back markers (empty segment), and deterministically decide whether the marker row belongs to the segment. States the CASES to cover, not a direction — so it reinforces what correct code already does. | BOUNDED — fires only on run/segment tasks; passing run/segment tasks score [1,1,1] (they already handle their boundaries), and the rule doesn't dictate include-vs-exclude, so it can't flip their semantics. |
| A | KNOWLEDGE + STRUCTURE (robustness) | prompt.md | New bullet in the RE-RUN block: the same code re-runs unattended on hidden inputs, so it must run to completion and reach the save on every one — an unexpected blank/text/date-as-string/shifted-header/row-count must not raise and abort before output_path is written; anticipate these (coerce, guard None, locate by header) and save at the very end, unconditionally, never inside a skippable branch. | BOUNDED — passing tasks score [1,1,1] on all 3 instances, so they never crash and never hit a default/guard path; the rule only changes behavior on inputs that would otherwise crash, which no passing task does. Phrased as "run to completion & always save" (robustness), NOT "default the cell" (which would risk silent wrong values). |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those exact inputs)
- 30930 (`[1,0,0]`): writes each count only when it hits a *closing* marker, so the trailing
  segment after the last "1" is never emitted; passes the preview arrangement, fails a
  hidden file whose data extends past the last marker. Edit B names exactly "the partial
  segment AFTER the last marker … still needs its result emitted."
- 32975 (`[1,0,0]`): running max reset per contiguous A-run; passes preview, fails variants
  → boundary/first-row-of-run handling. Edit B forces explicit handling of the run
  boundaries and the marker-row membership.
- 353-19 (`[1,0,1]`, case 2 no output): dynamic macro-style code raised on the hidden
  variant and never saved. Edit A makes "runs to completion and always writes output_path,
  unconditionally at the end" an explicit requirement — the exact failure mode.

## Confirmed-SAFE checks I ran
- Placeholders: grep of task_template.md shows all six required placeholders + {max_turns}
  intact; I did NOT touch task_template.md this iteration. prompt.md contains zero `{`/`}`.
- Both edits are ADDITIVE (a new bullet / an extended bullet); no existing rule was
  reworded toward a looser meaning, none deleted, no global decision/permission rule
  altered. Neither edit encodes a task id/value/date/answer — each states a rule over the
  input class.
- Regression reasoning is BEHAVIORAL: the 52 passing tasks score [1,1,1] on all three
  varying-data instances, so (Edit A) they never crash → the robustness guidance changes
  nothing they do, and (Edit B) their run/segment boundary handling is already correct →
  naming the cases to cover reinforces, does not flip, their logic.
- Did NOT re-add anything LEDGER/JOURNAL show was rejected; did NOT touch the "prefer
  literal values" line (5 passing tasks pass via formulas) or re-tighten verify item (a)
  (that caused the 399-14 regression under cand_0001).

## Process & features used
- Direct compact dumps of the 39 failing traces (instruction + answer_position + feedback +
  final emitted code) via a small read-only python script, avoiding the JSONL-transcript
  context overflow the prior iteration hit. Read the RRE-RUN code for the top gen-gap tasks
  to confirm the boundary hypothesis before editing. Read cand_0001/cand_0002 PROCESS +
  LEDGER + JOURNAL to avoid repeating harvested/rejected levers. No subagents needed at this
  scale.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- cand_0001's RE-RUN/generalization block + cand_0002's composite-key/blank-vs-zero/example
  blocks remain the load-bearing fixes — keep them.
- Do NOT ban Excel formulas globally (35747/37962/45581/49237/54675 pass via formulas).
- Do NOT re-tighten verify item (a) to "every cell holds a value" (399-14 regression).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why) — and the PLATEAU signal
- Comprehension / ambiguous-spec `[0,0,0]` cluster (the largest remaining, ~24 tasks): the
  agent's code already generalizes; it implements the WRONG operation. No general prose
  rule fixes a specific misreading without leaking a task-specific interpretation, and no
  gold is available in the traces to VERIFY a chosen direction — every such edit would fail
  the VERIFIED + SAFE tests. Padding the (already long) prompt with more abstract prose for
  a reader that is "less robust on long context" is the documented way to waste an
  iteration; I declined it.
- Volatile current-date (34-5, 32023): ambiguous snapshot vs today=2026-08-02.
- ENVIRONMENT/eval faults handed back (do NOT optimize against): 45944, 53062, 4225, 55258.
- PLATEAU: Δ has decayed +0.022 → +0.011 and the clean knowledge clusters are exhausted.
  Next lever if these two additive edits don't move the needle: a single tight WORKED
  EXAMPLE (SKILL menu item 5) — a canonical robust skeleton — is the remaining untried
  lever, but it must avoid encoding op-specific assumptions (e.g. never "clear the answer
  range first", which would reintroduce the 399-14 over-write). Beyond that the ceiling is
  the comprehension gap, which prose cannot safely close without gold.
